note: Thu 27 Aug 2026, ~08:05 SGT pre-Asia-open run (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30 SGT). Latest completed US session is Wednesday 26 Aug close; Nvidia's FQ2 print landed after that close and is the dominant overnight story heading into Thursday's Asia open. 6 of 14 items below are dated 25-26 Aug (last 24-48h), exceeding the freshness target -- Wednesday was a genuinely dense news day (PCE+GDP, NVDA earnings, Fed Governor Cook deadline, Iran-Oman/oil, gold/silver moves, BTC swings). SGX/Singapore-specific news was the thinnest category this run; the freshest available item (Aug 24 REIT/bank valuation read) is paired with slightly older (Aug 7-11) bank-earnings/STI-record context to keep it decision-relevant.

items.headline: Core PCE holds at 3.3% y/y, GDP confirmed at 1.5% -- markets tilt toward 'higher for longer,' not imminent cuts
items.summary: July core PCE (the Fed's preferred inflation gauge) rose 0.2% m/m and 3.3% y/y, in line with estimates but not falling toward the 2% target; headline PCE ran hotter at 3.7% y/y. Q2 GDP's second estimate held at 1.5% annualized (vs 2.1% in Q1), with durable goods orders beating at +1.1%. Major indices closed roughly flat as 10-year yields eased to ~4.63%, while money-market pricing shifted toward the Fed possibly holding rather than cutting in September given still-elevated inflation.
items.actionable: Sticky inflation plus fading cut odds argues against adding cash-pile duration bets and reinforces the case for holding the silver/miners hedge rather than trimming into strength.

items.headline: Nvidia crushes Q2 -- revenue $96.2B, guides to $108B, stock +14.5% after-hours
items.summary: Nvidia reported EPS of $2.22 and revenue of $96.2B (+106% y/y), with data-center sales of $89B beating estimates; guidance of $108B for the current quarter topped the $104.2B consensus. AWS separately announced a 2-million-GPU order using Nvidia's new Vera CPU. Shares jumped ~14.5% in after-hours trading, a strong signal for AI-capex sentiment heading into Thursday's Asia open.
items.actionable: A blowout NVDA print typically lifts HK tech/semis (SMIC, Tencent's AI-capex narrative) at Thursday's open -- worth watching 0981.HK and 0700.HK for a sympathy gap-up.

items.headline: Trump renews bid to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook; response deadline was today
items.summary: After the Supreme Court's June 29 ruling (5-4) that Cook could not be removed without due process, the White House sent a new removal letter citing unproven mortgage-fraud allegations and gave Cook until August 26 to submit evidence/argument in her defense. Cook's attorneys (Abbe Lowell, Norm Eisen) have denied the allegations; the case tests Fed independence directly ahead of the September rate decision.
items.actionable: An escalating Fed-independence fight is a structural tailwind for the gold/silver thesis (debasement/credibility hedge) even if it doesn't move September rate odds directly -- reinforces holding rather than fading the metals position.

items.headline: Iran and Oman float temporary Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor
items.summary: Omani FM Badr Albusaidi and Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi discussed a phased framework for a 'joint temporary navigational corridor' through Hormuz plus a mine-clearing project, following the strait's effective closure since Iran's war began in February 2026. The inbound route would run entirely through Iranian waters; outbound would cross both Iranian and Omani waters. Further talks are slated over the next 30-60 days toward a permanent arrangement.
items.actionable: Early-stage de-escalation reduces the geopolitical risk premium in oil and slightly dampens the 'crisis hedge' bid under gold -- a modest headwind for the precious-metals complex's safe-haven flows, though inflation/Fed drivers dominate.

items.headline: Oil falls below $81/bbl, third straight down session on Hormuz de-escalation
items.summary: WTI crude fell to $80.78/bbl, down 1.92% on the day and extending losses into a third consecutive session, directly attributed to the Iran-Oman corridor talks reducing near-term supply-disruption risk. This comes after months of elevated prices tied to the Hormuz closure since February.
items.actionable: No direct portfolio energy exposure, but falling oil eases one input into the 'hot inflation' narrative that has been supporting the silver/gold trade -- worth watching if it drags PCE-driven metals momentum.

items.headline: Gold pulls back from $4,730 intraday high to ~$4,675 after PCE data
items.summary: Gold opened above $4,700 for a second straight day, hit an intraday high of $4,730.90, then pulled back to $4,674.60/oz by mid-morning ET as the in-line-but-hot PCE print tempered near-term rate-cut hopes. This remains well below the January 2026 all-time record of $5,597.23 but continues a strong multi-week uptrend.
items.actionable: The pullback from intraday highs on hawkish-leaning data is a normal digestion move within an intact uptrend -- not yet a signal to reduce the gold-miner sleeve (GDX/NEM/GOLD).

items.headline: Silver notches its best month in years, up ~18% in August, holding near $68-69
items.summary: Silver traded at $68.73/oz on Aug 26 (September futures opened $68.63, down 0.1% from Tuesday), capping a monthly gain of roughly 17-18% -- its strongest month in recent memory and 78% higher year-over-year. This is well off the January 2026 record of $115.15 and the March contract's $79.70 spike, but the August rally has been driven by safe-haven and industrial-demand tailwinds.
items.actionable: The 18% August rally directly validates the levered silver position -- with the metal still ~40% below January's record, momentum and the gold/silver ratio compression argue for holding rather than taking profit here, though the pace of the run raises pullback risk after such a sharp monthly move.

items.headline: Barrick and Newmont settle Nevada Gold Mines dispute for $1.95B; Barrick advances North America IPO
items.summary: Barrick and Newmont resolved their outstanding Nevada Gold Mines joint-venture dispute, with Newmont paying Barrick $1.95B and both companies' Fourmile/Fiberline/Mike projects folded into the JV, the world's largest gold-mining complex. The settlement clears a hurdle for Barrick's planned IPO of its North American gold business by year-end 2026; separately Newmont confirmed 2026 guidance of 5.3M oz and launched a new $6B buyback.
items.actionable: Removal of a longstanding legal overhang plus a confirmed Barrick IPO catalyst is a fundamental (not just gold-price-driven) positive for the GDX/miner sleeve, distinct from the metals price momentum.

items.headline: Lynas Rare Earths misses FY profit estimates on 'painful' ramp-up costs, despite record revenue
items.summary: Lynas (ex-China's largest rare-earth refiner) reported FY net income of A$222.4M (vs A$8M prior year) but missed the A$263.2M consensus, with revenue up 76% to A$977.9M (US$717M) on surging non-China rare-earth prices. New interim CEO Le Roux (replacing retired Amanda Lacaze) cited ore-quality variability and processing complexity at the Western Australia operations as a 'very painful time.'
items.actionable: The earnings miss is operational, not demand-driven -- the underlying rare-earth pricing tailwind (relevant across MP/LYC.AX/UUUU/NEO watchlist) remains intact, but leadership transition and ramp-up risk argue for caution before adding to LYC.AX specifically.

items.headline: Xiaomi unveils self-developed Xring O3 AI chip to challenge Qualcomm
items.summary: Xiaomi launched its in-house Xring O3 mobile SoC, advancing its semiconductor self-sufficiency push with improved AI/image-processing capability. This follows Xiaomi's Q2 2026 results (reported Aug 18: revenue RMB 108.9B, adjusted net profit RMB 6.2B) and a raised full-year smartphone shipment target of 110M units.
items.actionable: In-house chip development reduces Xiaomi's long-term dependence on foreign silicon (mitigating export-control risk) but signals rising R&D/capex intensity similar to Tencent's margin-compressing AI spend -- a reason to watch margins closely rather than treat the chip news as a pure re-rating catalyst.

items.headline: SMIC Q2 revenue tops $3B for first time, beats on AI-driven chip demand
items.summary: SMIC posted Q2 2026 EPS of $0.06 (vs $0.0372 est.) and revenue of $3.01B (vs $2.85B est.), up 20% sequentially, with gross margin improving to 25.3% (+5.2pp q/q) on tight utilization and AI-related chip demand. Q3 guidance calls for 2-4% sequential revenue growth and gross margin rising to 26-28%.
items.actionable: Confirms mainland foundry demand is genuinely AI-driven and margin-accretive, not just cyclical -- supportive of holding SMIC through the current China-tech AI capex cycle, reinforced by Wednesday's NVDA beat.

items.headline: US weighing 7.5% 'overcapacity' tariff on China ahead of Xi-Trump summit
items.summary: The Trump administration is preparing a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods tied to manufacturing-overcapacity concerns, which would push cumulative China tariffs to roughly 20% -- a level officials believe stays within the bounds of the existing one-year trade truce. The move is calibrated to avoid derailing a planned Xi-Trump summit expected in late September 2026.
items.actionable: The tariff is deliberately sized to not blow up the truce/summit, so it should be a manageable, already-partially-priced-in headwind for HK tech rather than a reason to de-risk ahead of the Xi-Trump meeting.

items.headline: Bitcoin clears $80k for first time in 3+ months, then pulls back; Ether ETF inflows overtake Bitcoin's in August
items.summary: Bitcoin hit an intraday high of $81,235 on Tuesday Aug 25 (first close above $80k in over three months) before pulling back to $78,745.95 as of Wednesday morning ET, roughly flat to slightly down day-over-day. Separately, August marked the first month Ether ETF inflows ($3.87B) overtook Bitcoin ETF flows, which actually saw ~$750M in net outflows, amid a broader 'squeeze-led' rally across crypto.
items.actionable: The $80k break is a bullish technical signal, but the ETF-flow rotation into Ether suggests institutional demand is broadening beyond BTC -- not an immediate concern for a pure BTC position, but worth monitoring if outflows persist.

items.headline: Singapore banks/REITs: record Q2 bank profits and STI record high, REITs still trading at cheap yields
items.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB posted record/strong Q2 2026 profits (DBS S$3.08B +9%, OCBC S$2.22B +22% record, UOB S$1.48B +10%), helping drive the STI to a record intraday high of 5,774.21 on Aug 11 after Singapore's government raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 4.5-5.5%. As of Aug 24, Singapore REITs (including several Mapletree entities) remain among the highest dividend-yield names in the market (many above 6-9%), trading below book value even after the broader rally, while banks yield near 6%.
items.actionable: Bank earnings momentum and the STI record support holding DBS/OCBC, but REITs (Mapletree, KeppelREIT) remain the more rate-sensitive part of the SGX book -- the shift toward 'no Fed cut' in the PCE item above is a headwind specifically for that REIT sleeve even as banks stay resilient.
